entities.summary:
A Tobin tax was originally defined as a tax on all spot conversions of one currency into another. It was suggested by James Tobin, an economist who won the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences. Tobin's tax was originally intended to penalize short-term financial round-trip excursions into another currency. By the late 1990s, the term Tobin tax was being applied to all forms of short-term transaction taxation, whether across currencies or not.

The concept of the Tobin tax is being picked up by global institutions as a way to reduce speculative foreign exchange transactions. This has led to increased pressure on governments to implement such taxes. The European Union has taken steps to implement a financial transaction tax, which may be seen as an implementation of the Tobin tax.

The Tobin tax has been proposed as a way to reduce capital flight, promote financial stability, and increase tax revenues. However, its implementation has been met with resistance from the financial industry, which sees it as a barrier to trade and investment.

As the world becomes increasingly interconnected, the Tobin tax may become a more pressing issue. It could potentially lead to a reduction in financial turbulence and an increase in global economic stability.

'Ours is a world in which the partial, the particular, and the local are subordinated to the desires of the global and the universal.' - James Tobin
